Action.description:
The action of a rule (#34).

Each action is an object with a `type`, so options can be added later as
optional fields without a breaking change.

oneOf.description: Permit execution.
Block execution.
Record the match without changing the outcome.

anyOf.description: A string of at most 2048 bytes, with no control characters.

ControlLevel.description: Whether a class of object is controlled.

oneOf.description: Not evaluated.
Evaluated, and would-block decisions are reported only.
Evaluated and enforced.

Criterion.description:
A test of one fact about the object: `field operator values`.

Values are combined with OR for positive operators and with AND for
negative ones (#32): `not_in [a, b]` means neither `a` nor `b`.

case_sensitive.description:
Compare strings case-sensitively. Unset means the field's default
(#32), which is case-insensitive for every field defined so far.
Hashes and versions have no case, and reject this option.

values.description:
1 to 25 values. Each is at most 2048 bytes of UTF-8; the schema can
only bound the length in characters, so validation checks the bytes.

EnforcementOverride.description: How one rule relates to the policy mode (#36).

oneOf.description: Follow the effective mode. The default.
Enforce this rule even in audit or learning mode.
Never enforce this rule: it only reports what it would block.

Field.description:
The identity facts a criterion can test (#31).

This is the part of the #31 catalogue that has a matcher: hashes, the
signer, the path and the version resource. The other families (signer
constraints such as EKU and TBS hashes, packaged apps, installers,
ownership, origin and process relationships) arrive in later minor
versions, each with its facts and matcher.

oneOf.description: SHA-256 of the whole file. The primary identity (ADR 0008).
SHA-384 of the whole file.
SHA-512 of the whole file.

SHA-256 Authenticode image hash: the PE image without its checksum,
security directory entry and certificate table.
SHA-1 Authenticode image hash. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).

SHA-256 hash of the first page of the image, for OS-native policy
formats. It covers only that page, so it is a weak identity alone.

SHA-1 hash of the first page of the image. Compatibility only
(ADR 0008).

SHA-256 of an installer package with its timestamps left out, so
rebuilds of the same content share one value (#3).
SHA-1 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
MD5 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
The leaf signer's subject common name.
The common name of the leaf certificate's issuer.
The SHA-256 thumbprint of the leaf certificate.
The normalised full path.
The parent directory.
The on-disk file name.
The file extension, without its leading dot.
The original file name from the version resource.
The internal name from the version resource.
The file description from the version resource.
The product name from the version resource.
The company name from the version resource.
The file version from the version resource.
The product version from the version resource.

Match.description:
A condition tree (#33).

Each node is an object with exactly one key: `all`, `any`, `not` or
`criterion`.

oneOf.description: Matches when every child matches. Needs at least one child.
Matches when any child matches. Needs at least one child.
Matches when the child does not.
One test of one fact.

Metadata.description: Governance metadata (#40). More fields arrive with #40.

tags.description: Free-form labels, each 1 to 128 characters, at most 64.

Mode.description:
How a policy's decisions take effect (#36).

The variants are declared from weakest to strongest, so the derived
ordering ranks them. The "strictest" merge in #36 treats `learning` and
`audit` as equally strong; that rule belongs to the merge code, not to this
ordering.

oneOf.description: The engine is not consulted. The device is reported as unprotected.
Evaluate fully, allow everything, and report would-block decisions.
Like `monitor`, with a full event for every decision.
Audit, and report every would-block object as a learning candidate.
Decisions take effect: blocked means blocked.

ObjectType.description: The class of object being evaluated. Scripts are `script.<kind>`.

Operator.description:
How a criterion compares the fact with its values (#32). Positive
operators match if any value matches; negative operators (`not_*`)
match if no value does, and never match a fact that is unknown.

oneOf.description: Equal to any value.
Equal to none of the values.

Starts with any value. On paths, the value must end at a component
boundary: `C:\Tools` does not match `C:\ToolsX`.
Ends with any value.
Contains any value.
Contains none of the values.
Matches any wildcard pattern.
Matches none of the wildcard patterns.

Matches any regular expression. Anchored at both ends, and run by a
linear-time engine without look-around or backreferences.
Matches none of the regular expressions.
Version equal to any value.
Version greater than the value.
Version greater than or equal to the value.
Version less than the value.
Version less than or equal to the value.

Version within `[min, max]`, both inclusive. Takes exactly two
values, the minimum first.

Os.description:
The operating system a rule set targets. Other systems are reserved and
will be added in a minor version.

oneOf.description: Windows.

Policy.description: The decision part of a policy: which rule sets apply, and how.

id.description: Stable ID. Renaming the policy never changes it.

name.description:
Display name: 1 to 128 characters, trimmed, no control characters.
Uniqueness within a tenant is checked by the server (#10).

precedence_model.description: How matching rules are combined (#35, ADR 0004).

revision.description: Monotonic revision, raised by the server on every change (#10).

rule_sets.description: The rule sets that apply, in order, by ID.

settings.description: Typed settings. Every field has a documented default.

PolicyId.description: The stable ID of a policy.

PolicySettings.description:
Settings that apply to the whole policy. Every field is optional in a
document and has the default shown in the schema.

advanced.description:
Engineering settings, checked against a registry of known keys. The
registry is empty in this version, so any key is rejected unless
`allow_unknown_advanced` is set.

allow_unknown_advanced.description: Accept keys in `advanced` that the registry does not know.

capture_command_line.description:
Whether the agent records process command lines. Off by default for
privacy (#18).

decision_cache_ttl_secs.description: How long a decision may be cached, in seconds. `0` disables the cache.

max_ancestor_depth.description: How many ancestors process criteria may inspect (#31).

override_durations.description:
Durations, in minutes, offered for override sessions (#9). At most 5
slots, each at most 10080. `0` marks a disabled slot.

script_control.description: Control level for scripts of a kind not listed in `script_control_by_kind`.

script_control_by_kind.description: Control level per script kind, overriding `script_control`.

PrecedenceModel.description:
How the matching rules of the ordinary rule sets are combined (#35).

The mandatory-deny tier and the implicit deny for unmatched files apply
under every model (ADR 0004).

oneOf.description: Any matching deny blocks; otherwise any matching allow allows. The default.
Any matching allow allows. Not recommended for Essential Eight.
The rule with the most specific identity wins.
Rules are ordered, and the first match decides.
The rule with the winning numeric priority decides.

Rule.description: One rule: a match tree and the action taken when it matches.

display_id.description: Human short ID from the tenant's sequence, `R-` and 6 to 12 digits.

enabled.description: Disabled rules are kept, but never decide.

name.description: Display name, with the same rules as a policy name.

object_types.description: The object classes the rule applies to. Empty means every class.

RuleId.description: The stable ID of a rule. It is never reused, even after the rule is deleted.

RuleSet.description: A named, reusable, ordered collection of rules.

kind.description: What the rule set is for.

mandatory.description:
Only for `blocklist`: evaluated in the non-overridable mandatory-deny
tier (#35, ADR 0004).

name.description: Display name, with the same rules as a policy name.

os.description: The operating system the rules are written for.

read_only.description: Curated sets are read-only: edit a duplicate instead.

version.description: The content version of this rule set, for display (for example `3.0`).

RuleSetId.description: The stable ID of a rule set.

RuleSetKind.description: The purpose of a rule set.

oneOf.description: Rules that allow.
Rules that deny.
A baseline of what was present at a point in time.
Trusted sources (#9).
Elevation rules (#12).
Containment rules (#14).
Any mix of actions.

SchemaVersion.description: A semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, without pre-release or build suffixes.

TimeZoneBasis.description: The clock that schedules are interpreted in.

oneOf.description: The device's local time zone.
Coordinated Universal Time.

Uuid7.description: A UUID version 7 in canonical lowercase form.

description: A versioned policy document: one policy and the rule sets it uses.

rule_sets.description:
The rule sets the policy references, in any order. The policy's
`rule_sets` list gives the order that applies.

schema_version.description:
The version of this schema the document was written for. A reader
accepts the same major version and any minor version.
